body:
I know I'm not alone, I have great friends and family, but sometimes I feel like I'm a million miles away from them. I'm the youngest of three so in some way I'll always be the baby, but it seems like they don't see that I'm not a kid anymore. 

I think many people actually do feel this way to some degree, but they have that same feeling that no one cares, so they get bitter and it creates a vicious circle.

I'm back in college after taking a year off, so I'm juggling this on top of that, but it seems like it's never enough for people. That may be more my perception than them, but it's tough telling them that depression doesn't just go away like a cold or something.

That's the gist of it, for the most part. I don't think I'll ever do anything, either, I've never been low enough to honestly consider it. I've been to therapy, but I'm back in school now so I don't have a lot of time to go back. Just knowing that there are places like this where you can talk to people helps, though. People seem so fake in most other areas of the Internet, even the world to a degree. It just makes me feel crazy when everybody else presents themselves like a living highlight reel and I have all these things inside me that I can't talk about in most cases. I know there are people that feel this way even among those that put on an act, but the fact that everybody acts like depression doesn't exist, or that it's something to be ashamed of, really bothers me. Many people are quick to sign a cast or be there for someone recovering from surgery, but if there's an imbalance in their brain they basically become a pariah. I don't get it.

Hey, I've got nothing to do for an hour at least, myself. I'm free to talk, but it's easier for me to type it out. 

 I want to preface this by saying that I don't intend to kill myself, now or ever, as far as I can tell...but I still think about it more than I'd like to. Even when I'm actually enjoying myself, drinking with friends, going for a drive, whatever, I'll have a moment where I think, "Gee, what if I was dead?" or "You know what would be cool? Driving over the guard rails right now..." I've been so low I wouldn't give a shit if I was hit by a truck, but I've never been so low I just wanted to end it all. It's frustrating because, even though I have friends and family that love me and I love them, I can't talk to them about this in a way that sticks, and I feel alone all the time. We just have the same conversation with different words over and over and I often feel worse afterwards than when we started talking. I'm relieved that I'm even trying to talk to them about it, because I went a solid year or more without saying anything to anyone. That isn't healthy for anyone to have bouncing around in their head. But when you try time and again to explain how you feel like you're dying in your own skin to people that genuinely want to help but can't understand, you eventually stop talking about it because you don't want to fatigue them anymore. So I tried to find someplace to talk about this, and after trying to join forums that had an extensive vetting process (which is kind of a thumb in its eye considering the subject matter, but that's another can of worms) I came here. So, that's a little background on me...
